World.title: What it means to be a hostile witness in Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

ZULEIKA LOPEZ. Vice President Sara Duterte's Chief of Staff Atty. Zuleika Lopez attends the House committee on good government and public accountability hearing on the alleged fund misuse of Duterte on November 20, 2024.

A 'hostile' witness is a formal designation that changes how he or she is treated in court. Zuleika Lopez is one such witness.

When Vice President Sara Duterte’s chief of staff Zuleika Lopez takes the witness stand, she will be the first hostile witness in the impeachment trial of Duterte.

It’s not a mere modifier to refer to an antagonistic person called by the party for direct examination, but a formal designation that changes how they are treated in court.

The Senate’s existing impeachment rules do not make mention of the phrase “hostile witness” but say “the revised Rules of Court shall apply suppletorily whenever applicable.”

Section 13 of the 2019 amendments to the 1989 Rules of Evidence states that the court can declare a witness as unwilling or hostile “upon adequate showing of his or her adverse interest, unjustified reluctance to testify, or his or her having misled the party into calling him or her to the witness stand.”

What happens after her status as a hostile witness is formalized?

“The examiner, the one presenting her, would be able to ask leading questions,” public prosecutor Leila de Lima told Rappler in an interview. “She is expected to be a hostile witness and therefore she has to be handled accordingly.”

Play Video

Under Section 10 of the Rules of Evidence, an unwilling or hostile witness may be subjected to leading and misleading questions. Normally, during direct examination of witnesses, they cannot be asked such questions.

“The unwilling or hostile witness so declared, or the witness who is an adverse party, may be impeached by the party presenting him or her in all respects as if he or she had been called by the adverse party, except by evidence of his or her bad character. He or she may also be impeached and cross-examined by the adverse party, but such cross-examination must only be on the subject matter of his or her examination-in-chief,” reads Section 13 of the said guidelines.

In the context of rules of evidence, to impeach someone means to challenge their credibility.

“There will be preliminary questions to establish her being a hostile witness, then leading questions, because it is through leading questions that you’re able to really extract direct answers,” De Lima said.

Lopez was the reason for Duterte’s visit to the House of Representatives first on November 21, 2024, when the Vice President locked herself inside her brother’s office and then days later held the infamous virtual media conference where she threatened the life of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Play Video

Lopez at the time was detained at the House after being cited in contempt during a House good government committee inquiry into Duterte’s alleged fund misuse.

Duterte’s outburst was triggered when Lopez, during the online Zoom press conference on November 23, had a meltdown after the House ordered her transfer to the Women’s Correctional Facility in Mandaluyong City.

Lopez was supposed to be the only one giving the unauthorized press conference from her detention cell but Duterte took over after her chief of staff suffered an anxiety attack. – Rappler.com

World.title: [Vantage Point] The strategic value of the CBK privatization
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

The undisputed ownership of the CBK complex may ultimately prove to be one of the most rewarding, defensive, and forward-looking corporate victories of modern-day energy transition

In case you missed my previous newsletters that also tackled the Caliraya-Botocan-Kalayaan (CBK) project, do check them out here and here.

The Aboitiz group’s tactical acquisition of the CBK hydroelectric complex via a P36.27-billion bid by the Thunder Consortium represents a profound structural positioning within the future architecture of the Luzon electricity grid.

MODEL. Aboitiz Power chairman Sabin Aboitiz shows President Ferdinand Marcos a 3D model of the Caliraya-Botocan-Kalayaan Hydroelectric Power Plant during the turnover of the power plant on February 9, 2026 in Laguna. Photo by Presidential Communications Office

It transcends far beyond a simple asset expansion or a premium driven by conventional corporate rivalry.

Superficial market analyses frequently mischaracterize the true nature of this transaction by focusing exclusively on the short-term financial premium paid over competing offers, or by evaluating it through the outdated lens of standard infrastructure acquisitions that merely seek to aggregate legacy generation capacity.

A more rigorous structural assessment of the transaction shows that the Aboitiz group was not purchasing yesterday’s conventional power plant, but was instead deliberately securing a foundational long-term stake in tomorrow’s modernized electricity infrastructure.



Let’s examine the macroeconomic shift in power system economics over the past decade — an evolution that has fundamentally transformed how electricity is generated, distributed, priced, and valued across both global and domestic markets.

The traditional utility model used to rely on a linear framework where centralized assets generated stable power for utility distribution, and grid reliability depended on maintaining enough reserve capacity to meet forecasted demand.

This functioned with remarkable efficiency as long as the grid was dominated by dispatchable baseload sources such as coal, oil, natural gas, geothermal, and conventional reservoir hydro facilities. All of these allowed engineers and operators to forecast supply and demand with a high degree of mathematical accuracy.

Disruptions in the grid

However, the rapid rise of solar and wind power disrupted the traditional grid because renewable energy is intermittent. Solar output can drop instantly when a cloud passes, even though consumer demand stays the same.

Today, the main challenge for modern power systems is no longer just generating electricity, but keeping the grid balanced and stable in real time. Globally, this shift lowers the value of basic power generation, while making flexible, on-demand energy storage and grid balancing services much more valuable.

This explains the immense strategic premium and long-term utility of the CBK complex. Unlike standard run-of-river or traditional hydroelectric facilities, it possesses unique pumped-storage capabilities .

During periods of low grid demand and abundant baseline supply, the facility utilizes excess electricity from the network to pump water into its elevated reservoirs, effectively acting as a giant, grid-scale utility battery that absorbs surplus power when it is least valued by the market. Conversely, when grid demand spikes sharply or variable renewable generation drops unexpectedly, this stored water is rapidly released through high-capacity turbines to generate and dispatch electricity almost immediately back into the grid.

HYDRO. A section of the Caliraya-Botocan-Kalayaan (CBK) Hydroelectric Power Plant Complex in Laguna now under the Thunder Consortium, a partnership among Aboitiz Renewables, Sumitomo Corp. and J-Power. The power plant is the Philippines’ largest pumped-storage hydro facility which helps stabilize the Luzon grid. Photo courtesy of Aboitiz Power Corp.



TOP. A bird’s eye view of the 789-MW Caliraya-Botocan-Kalayaan (CBK) Hydroelectric Power Plant Complex in Laguna in February 2026. Photo courtesy of Aboitz Power Corp.

Long before lithium-ion batteries became popular or commercially viable, pumped-storage facilities were already balancing the power grid on a massive scale. These assets are highly protected from future competition because they are nearly impossible to duplicate. This is due to a lack of suitable geographic locations, highly complex environmental permit application processes, and the massive upfront funding required to build them.

Aboitiz Power Corporation’s aggressive and forward-looking bidding behavior reflects a sophisticated alignment of corporate capability with these inevitable long-term macroeconomic and regulatory trends.

Historically anchored in thermal generation assets, the company has been deliberately executing a structural transition toward a diversified portfolio, recognizing that the future of electricity belongs to operators capable of integrating multiple energy sources while maintaining strict grid reliability.

Aboitiz Power also has a robust capital structure backed by recurring, reliable income streams from its distribution utilities and mature generation assets, giving it the balance-sheet resilience required to deploy patient capital into projects with exceptionally lengthy development and payback horizons.

While the Philippine renewable transition is still in its early stages and has not yet reached the critical tipping point where balancing constraints dominate everyday policy discussions, that inflection point is rapidly approaching as more solar and wind projects hook into the national network.

When variable renewable penetration triggers a greater market need for immediate frequency regulation and rapid dispatch, assets like CBK will command a lucrative, privileged position within the domestic electricity ecosystem.

The historical trajectory of the CBK complex reflects the broader evolution of the Philippine power sector itself, moving seamlessly from an era focused on solving absolute generation capacity deficits to a modern landscape defined entirely by the management of grid complexity and resilience.

High stakes, long term

Decades ago, the visionary engineers of Argentina’s Industrias Metalúrgicas Pescarmona Sociedad Anónima (IMPSA) recognized CBK’s long-duration strategic value, followed closely by institutional Japanese infrastructure investors who valued its exceptionally stable and recurring cash flows.

By making an even larger corporate wager on this asset today, the Aboitiz group is placing a high-stakes, long-term call option on the future operating system of the entire Luzon grid. Its wager is that CBK’s systemic importance will grow exponentially as the energy transition accelerates over the next ten years.

Ultimately, the fiercest competition in the Philippine energy sector is no longer about which conglomerate can generate the most raw electricity, but about who controls the critical nodes that keep the grid stable when renewable power becomes the dominant source of supply.

In this context, the undisputed ownership of the CBK complex may ultimately prove to be one of the most rewarding, defensive, and forward-looking corporate victories of modern-day energy transition.

I welcome your views on these and other issues where decisions made in power shape the country’s economic future.

World.title: Prosecutors justify Sara Duterte bank records request as ‘unedited truth’
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

TRIAL. The Senate opened the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte convening as an impeachment court with 21 senator-judges present in the session hall, on July 6, 2026.

The prosecution team, among other arguments, insists that the documents they seek are relevant even though they predate Duterte's vice presidency

The prosecution team in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte filed its memorandum with the impeachment court, explaining why it needs to obtain her bank and tax records.

The submission came after impeachment court presiding officer Chiz Escudero directed the prosecution and defense teams to present their arguments in writing ahead of the oral arguments scheduled for July 15.

Rappler obtained a copy of the document filed by the prosecution on July 13. The prosecution presented the following arguments.

‘Documents relevant’

The prosecution is requesting Duterte’s bank records, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) records, and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records.

Many of these documents predate her vice presidency, but the prosecution says they are relevant because “they do not merely target completed historical acts, but rather an active, in-term violation of anti-graft laws and accountability.”

“By continuously retaining, enjoying, and failing to truthfully disclose these hidden assets in her current SALN submissions as vice president, the respondent is actively committing a live, ongoing breach of public trust during her tenure,” the prosecution argued.

The prosecution also tried to undermine the defense team’s reliance on Duterte v House, the 2025 Supreme Court ruling that declared her first impeachment by the House as unconstitutional. In that ruling, the Court stated: “The basis of any charge must be for impeachable acts or omissions committed in relation to their office and during the current term of the impeachable officer.”

The prosecution, however, invoked the legal concept of obiter dictum, which refers to a court’s incidental observations that are not binding precedents.

“The Duterte case strictly addressed a procedural violation regarding the one-year filing bar; it never substantively interpreted Article XI, Section 2, nor did it explain how a temporal limitation could be derived from a constitutional text that completely lacks one,” the prosecution said.

‘Numerous laws don’t prevent the issuance of subpoena’

There are numerous laws that would make the Senate impeachment court — and even the House justice committee back in April — second-guess itself when it comes to accessing Duterte’s financial records.

But the prosecution asserted that these laws do not prevent agencies from releasing the documents they wanted.

On the Bank Secrecy Law: The prosecution said the measure “expressly recognizes cases of impeachment as one of the exceptions” to the disclosure of, or inquiry into, deposits.

On the Anti-Money Laundering Act: The prosecution said its confidentiality clause pertains to disclosure of information acquired by AMLC officers, but should “not be construed as creating an absolute evidentiary privilege that categorically disables a constitutionally constituted impeachment tribunal from compelling the production of relevant records pursuant to lawful process.”

On the National Internal Revenue Code: Section 270 of the NIRC penalizes BIR officers who disclose confidential taxpayer information, but the prosecution said the law “does not create an absolute prohibition against the production of tax records,” adding that the measure “recognizes that disclosure may be made when authorized by law.”

On the Data Privacy Act: The prosecution insisted that the DPA “does not create an absolute privilege against production of documents containing personal information pursuant to lawful process.”

Unique constitutional proceeding

The prosecution argued that the 1987 Constitution did not task the judiciary but the Senate to try an impeached official, indicating that it is “not an ordinary lawsuit.”

“It is the Constitution’s highest mechanism of public accountability, deliberately entrusted to a body that need not be composed entirely of lawyers and therefore is not confined by the same rigid technicalities that govern ordinary courts.”

The prosecution, nonetheless, maintained that their subpoena requests satisfy the requirements under the Rules of Court.

“A subpoena duces tecum does not require a prior showing that the documents sought will conclusively establish the allegations. At this stage, the relevant inquiries are whether the requested documents are relevant and material to the issues before the tribunal,” the prosecution said.

The prosecution quoted Escudero during his opening day speech when he talked about how the rules should be “construed liberally” so that Filipinos “may hear the whole and impartial truth.”

“The whole truth. Those words deserve emphasis, not because they are eloquent, but because they capture the purpose of the proceeding. Not the convenient truth. Not the edited truth. Not the portion that survives procedural reluctance. But the whole truth,” the document reads.

“And truth, by its nature, arrives in fragments.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Bonoan immunity deal faces Sandiganbayan test
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

The hearing is scheduled at 1:30 pm Tuesday, July 14, before the Sandiganbayan’s 2nd Division

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman will make a crucial push on Tuesday, July 14, for its immunity deal with former Public Works secretary Manuel Bonoan, as prosecutors ask the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan to allow an amended charge sheet removing him as an accused.

The hearing is scheduled at 1:30 pm before the Sandiganbayan’s 2nd Division. If granted, Senator Jinggoy Estrada will remain as the sole defendant in the case involving alleged misuse of public works funds.

The original charge sheet filed on May 28 accused Estrada and Bonoan of violating the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act for allegedly causing government losses by diverting over P213 million, or 25% of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) budget for infrastructure projects in Bulacan.

It was alleged that Estrada sought P355 million for the province’s 1st District and another P500 million for its remaining districts, with 25% of the allocations allegedly returned as kickbacks.

Prosecutors alleged that the projects were inserted into the National Expenditure Program, the House of Representatives’ version of the budget, the bicameral conference committee report and eventually the 2025 national budget.

The 5th Division of the Sandiganbayan is also set to hear on Wednesday, July 15, a similar motion seeking to remove Bonoan as an accused in separate plunder and graft cases.

That case also involves allegations that Estrada received P350 million in kickbacks from irregular infrastructure contracts in Metro Manila and Oriental Mindoro. Investigators said the amount represented 25% of DPWH funds requested by the senator for flood control and other public works projects.

Under court rules, the decision to discharge an accused from a case rests with the Sandiganbayan. The removal of Bonoan as a defendant is being pursued through an amended information, which prosecutors said is allowed because he has yet to be arraigned in any of the cases.

The proposed amendment follows Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla’s announcement on June 29 that prosecutors had reached an agreement with Bonoan, who would cooperate in other government cases and testify as a state witness.

Remulla said Bonoan could provide important information because, as a former DPWH secretary, he had knowledge of discussions involving lawmakers’ budget requests and alleged insertions.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said Bonoan initiated the arrangement after sending Remulla a letter in early June offering information that could implicate several lawmakers. – Rappler.com

World.title: Alex Eala delighted by warm Marcos reception: ‘I feel very seen’
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

SPECIAL GUEST. Filipina tennis star Alex Eala with her parents Mike and Rizza, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos at Malacañang on July 13, 2026.

Filipina tennis ace Alex Eala promises to continue representing the Philippines in the 'best way’ after receiving the Presidential Citation at Malacañang

MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala never imagined she would be hosted by the Philippine president and honored for her hard work.

Eala enjoyed a rousing reception from President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. at Malacañang and received the Presidential Citation on Monday night, July 13, as she returned home following her historic run in the Wimbledon Championship.

Marcos hailed the 21-year-old tennis star as the embodiment of the Filipinos’ greatest qualities.

“Thank you, Mr. President, for this special honor and for the warm welcome. Never in my wildest dreams would I have thought that I would be having dinner here at the Malacañang Palace next to you and be receiving such kind and genuine words. I feel very seen,” said Eala in her speech.

“Hearing that come from you, I feel like all the hard work that I’ve done is seen. All the hours that aren’t on TV are seen and validated and appreciated, so thank you so, so much.”

In Wimbledon, Eala dethroned Poland’s Iga Swiatek to reach the fourth round, becoming the first Filipino to make the second week of a Grand Slam.

That splendid campaign propelled Eala to a new career-high ranking of No. 28 as she cracked the top 30 for the third time this year, establishing herself as one of the players to watch out for on the tour.

For Eala, her achievements are as much as the Philippines’ as they are hers.

“I’m so grateful that I’m able to share my triumphs, most especially my most recent run at Wimbledon, with the country,” said Eala.

“I cannot begin to describe how overjoyed I am to see how my progress has been received by the Filipino people, and it warms my heart because I know that it comes from a profound and shared love for our nation.”

“With that being said, I’m deeply proud to be Filipino. I carry the flag with me wherever I go and I am a firm believer that where you come from is a big part of who you are.”

And as Eala soon returns to action after her relatively brief homecoming, she vows to keep showcasing the best of the country, on and off the court.

“I promise that I will continue to represent the Philippines in the best way that I possibly can,” Eala said. – Rappler.com

World.title: Oil climbs to one-month high as US, Iran step up attacks
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

TANKERS IN GULF. Tankers sail in the Gulf, near the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from northern Ras al-Khaimah, near the border with Oman’s Musandam governance, amid the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, in United Arab Emirates, March 11, 2026.

Oil prices are now at their highest since the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to end the war on June 17

Oil prices rose 2% on Tuesday, July 14, to their highest in four weeks, as the US reimposed its naval blockade of Iran while the two countries stepped up attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, heightening uncertainty about energy flows.

Brent crude futures LCOc1 climbed $1.68, or 2%, to $84.98 per barrel by 0051 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude CLc1 rose $1.65, or 2.1%, to $79.79 a barrel. Brent crude surged 9.6% in the previous session, its biggest daily gain since May 2020.

Oil prices are now at their highest since the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to end the war on June 17.

Two United Arab Emirates tankers were hit by two Iranian cruise missiles in the southern lane of the Strait of Hormuz in Omani territorial waters, the UAE Ministry of Defense said on Monday, July 13, killing one Indian crew member and wounding eight others.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump told reporters that the United States had reinstated its blockade of Iranian shipping, adding that he wanted the US to be reimbursed for protecting countries that it was helping in the Strait of Hormuz.

“The latest escalation, including the US reinstatement of the blockade and Iranian responses, has clearly injected fresh risk into the market,” KCM Trade chief market analyst Tim Waterer said.

“While a full closure hasn’t occurred, the competing objectives of both sides have made the supply picture highly uncertain,” he added.

US Central Command said it began a third consecutive night of strikes against Iran, while Tehran’s semi-official YJC news agency said early on Tuesday that seven explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas and two more on Kish Island.

Elsewhere, Yemen’s Houthi movement fired missiles at Saudi Arabia after accusing the kingdom of bombing an airport under its control on Monday.

“If the Houthis extend their attacks to Saudi’s crude products in the Red Sea, it could put (further) uncertainties on crude flows from the region,” Simon Wong, a portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said in a note.

Meanwhile, US crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week, while gasoline and distillate stocks likely rose, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Monday. – Rappler.com

World.title: Prosecutors question Sara Duterte’s fitness to be president
World.content:
President Sara Duterte. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte’s fitness for the presidency was put in question on Tuesday as impeachment prosecutors raised concerns on her temperament over her violent threats against President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr.

In a media briefing, Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon said it was unacceptable for the nation to have a leader who either “lies in front of the people” or “contracts a killer,” referring to Duterte’s profanity-laden outburst against Marcos and his family.

Duterte, who is facing an impeachment trial in the Senate, faces an array of accusations that she misused hundreds of millions in confidential funds, amassed unexplained wealth and threatened the lives of Marcos, the First Lady, and his cousin, a former speaker of the House of Representatives.

Article continues after this 

“Is this the kind of president that we want? A vice president that lies or a vice president that contracts a killer,” Ridon said.

READ: Prosecutors to scrutinize Sara Duterte’s fitness for office

A scion of a popular political family, Duterte has emerged as a strong contender for the presidency, buoyed by a loyal base that keeps her appeal intact even amid swirling controversy that has led to her being impeached twice in her four years in office.

Duterte announced her plan to run in 2028 after efforts to remove her from office resurfaced in February.

“I don’t think it is acceptable to the people that you have a vice president that lies in front of the people, or a vice president that contracts a killer,” said Ridon, an impeachment prosecutor.

Article continues after this 

Duterte’s lawyers on Monday denied that the vice president hired an assassin to kill Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta Marcos and former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez in the event that she were killed.

Manila Rep. Joel Chua, also an impeachment prosecutor, echoed Ridon’s sentiment in a separate statement, saying that Duterte’s outburst – which stemmed from an order to transfer her chief-of-staff to a jail after being detained by lawmakers in the House for “undue interference” – raised questions over her disposition and ability to keep her emotions in check.

Article continues after this 

“What if the time comes that she becomes president, and an incident happens to her staff. Does that mean she’ll unleash her wrath on anyone because she is angry?” Chua asked in Filipino.

Prosecutors need at least two-thirds of the Senate to convict Duterte, a verdict that would remove her from office and may also carry a perpetual ban from holding public office for life. /mr

World.title: Marcoleta undergoes independent medical exam at PGH amid plunder case
World.content:
Sen. Rodante Marcoleta (center) arrives in a wheelchair at the University of the Philippines–Philippine General Hospital in Manila on Tuesday, July 14, 2026, to undergo an independent medical examination. (Photo by Mary Joy Salcedo/INQUIRER)

MANILA, Philippines — Wearing handcuffs and a detainee shirt under a protective vest, Sen. Rodante Marcoleta arrived at the University of the Philippines–Philippine General Hospital (UP-PGH) in a wheelchair to undergo an independent medical examination.

The examination was ordered by the Sandiganbayan to determine whether his continued confinement at the PNP General Hospital in Camp Crame, Quezon City, remains necessary amid his plunder case.

Marcoleta’s medical examination was scheduled to begin at noon.

Article continues after this 

MARCOLETA AT UP-PGHWATCH: Wearing handcuffs and a detainee shirt under a protective vest, Sen. Rodante Marcoleta arrives here at the University of the Philippines–Philippine General Hospital on a wheelchair to undergo an independent medical + pic.twitter.com/wdQlVqsGKJ — MJ Salcedo (@MJSalcedoINQ) July 14, 2026

The senator is facing a non-bailable plunder case in connection with an alleged P75 million in undeclared campaign donations during the 2025 elections.

On July 6, the Sandiganbayan issued an arrest warrant against Marcoleta and his three co-accused.

READ: PNP: Marcoleta stable ahead of July 14 PGH exam

Instead of being taken to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas, Quezon City, Marcoleta was admitted to the PNP General Hospital after reportedly experiencing chest pains, high blood pressure, and mild pneumonia.

Following his examination at UP-PGH, the Sandiganbayan ordered the hospital to submit a medical report on Wednesday on the senator’s condition.

Article continues after this 

READ: Sandiganbayan to PNP: Bring Marcoleta to PGH for exam, then to court

The anti-graft court also ordered the PNP to bring Marcoleta to his hearing on Wednesday. /mcm

World.title: Zaldy Co’s co-accused stresses ‘voluntary surrender’ in court
World.content:
Juliet Calvo (inset), former Department of Public Works and Highways Mimaropa maintenance division chief, attends her arraignment before the Sandiganbayan on December 2, 2025. — Photo by Faith Argosino/INQUIRER.net

MANILA, Philippines — The defense and prosecution on Tuesday both agreed that the co-accused of former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co presented herself to the police before the issuance of a warrant of arrest.

The camp of former public works engineer Juliet Calvo made the offer for stipulation during Sandiganbayan’s Sixth Division trial of her and co-accused’s non-bailable malversation of public funds case over an anomalous Oriental Mindoro project.

Calvo’s counsel Edwin Labro Jr. offered for stipulation her “voluntary surrender” to the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) on Nov. 5, 2025.

Article continues after this 

READ: Ombudsman files 1st batch of raps vs Zaldy Co, others before Sandigan

Under Article 13, Paragraph 7 of the Revised Penal Code, an offender’s voluntary surrender before authorities could be considered as one of mitigating circumstances.

Associate Justice Sarah Jane Fernandez, Sixth Division chairperson, asked the counsel to specify the manner in which she surrendered.

Labro noted that Calvo presented herself to the officers of CIDG Metro Manila “to turn herself in and allow herself to be taken into custody.”

Calvo’s lawyer also offered for stipulation the certification from CIDG Metro Manila regional director Col. John Guiagui stating that Calvo voluntarily surrendered in anticipation of a warrant of arrest.

Article continues after this 

State prosecutor Madonna Lyn Casares said the prosecution stipulated the authenticity of the CIDG certification, and that Calvo presented herself without a police escort.

With the stipulation, Labro said they will withdraw the motion for the subpoena for Guiagui to testify.

Article continues after this 

“How wonderful, that makes our proceedings more efficient,” said Sixth Division Member Associate Justice Lord Villanueva.

The non-bailable malversation of funds through falsification of public documents stemmed from a P289.4 million worth Sunwest project — or the company where Co is said to be a beneficial owner — which state prosecutors said was found to have serious structural deficiencies.

For his part, Co could not participate in the trial as he was earlier declared by Sandiganbayan as a fugitive from justice.

A respondent declared as a fugitive from justice could no longer participate in the proceedings and could not seek any judicial relief unless they surrender voluntarily.

Sunwest is co-founded by Co, who also used to be the chairperson of the powerful House committee on appropriations before his resignation as a party-list representative in September last year amid the widespread public outrage on the multibillion flood control corruption scandal. /das

World.title: PNP stands by Marcoleta medical findings amid separate PGH exam
World.content:
Wearing handcuffs and a detainee shirt under a protective vest, Sen. Rodante Marcoleta arrives at the University of the Philippines–Philippine General Hospital in a wheelchair to undergo an independent medical examination on Tuesday, July 14, 2026. — Screengrab from a video by Mary Joy Salcedo/INQUIRER.net

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday defended its findings on Sen. Rodante Marcoleta’s medical condition as he was ordered by the Sandiganbayan to undergo a separate medical examination by the Philippine General Hospital (PGH).

“Rather than doubting the evaluation of our doctors here, the Sandiganbayan did this to erase the public’s doubts,” PNP public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co told reporters in Camp Crame.

“We stand by our doctors here. They will not gamble with their future, with their careers. They have no reason for us to doubt,” he stressed.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP brings Marcoleta to PGH for exam after Sandiganbayan order

Marcoleta was arrested last July 6 over a plunder case in connection with a P75-million donation he received but did not declare when he was a party-list representative before his 2025 senatorial bid.

However, he was taken to the PNP General Hospital (PNPGH) in Camp Crame after reportedly experiencing chest pains.

Doctors at the PNPGH subsequently said the senator was experiencing mild pneumonia and degenerative disc disease, a condition related to the spine, a week after he was arrested for plunder.

On Tuesday morning, Marcoleta was taken to the PGH in Manila on Tuesday morning to assess whether he still needed to be confined at the PNPGH.

Article continues after this 

“Just like any other detention facility… it is incumbent upon us that, whenever someone in our custody has an illness, of course, what else will we do but to bring them to the hospital?” Co maintained.

“Our rules here provide that there are no VIP rooms. We only have the normal rooms, so that’s where we brought him and that’s where he is recovering,” he added.

Article continues after this 

Co noted that the PNP has yet to determine what medical exams will be done for Marcoleta and what time he will be returned to the PNPGH. /das

World.title: Consumer group: Schools must keep up with AI, other tech advancements
World.content:
REUTERS FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — Consumer advocacy group CitizenWatch Philippines on Tuesday called on the government to fast-track the integration of digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), into learning as part of efforts to improve the country’s education system.

In a statement, CitizenWatch Philippines said the government, telecommunications companies, and schools must coordinate to ensure the country’s education system keeps pace with advancements in the digital economy.

The group noted that the Philippines was recently classified as an upper-middle-income country, citing broad-based expansion that included improvements in digital infrastructure.

Article continues after this 

READ: Gov’t, development lenders urged to invest in PH’s digital infrastructure

It cited the launch of satellite-to-mobile services by Globe Telecom in partnership with Starlink last June, following approval from the National Telecommunications Commission, allowing connectivity in areas where traditional cell towers cannot reach.

“Government and industry have moved with real intent on infrastructure—fiber, 5G, data centers, AI-ready networks. That progress deserves recognition,” CitizenWatch co-convenor Kit Belmonte said.

“The opportunity now is to bring education reform into that same rhythm so investment in connectivity and learning advances together rather than on separate timelines,” he added.

These investments align with the government’s policy framework, with Belmonte noting that the Philippine Development Plan 2023–2028 identifies digital education and infrastructure as key strategies for national transformation. He added that the 2026–2028 Strategic Investment Priority Plan also classifies digital education projects as a priority area for incentives.

Article continues after this 

READ: CitizenWatch urges DILG to streamline telco permit rules

Belmonte said “one of the clearest opportunities” is the use of AI in the classroom as a learning tool, noting that it can help teachers support students who learn at different paces.

Article continues after this 

“AI-powered personalized learning, adaptive assessments, and intelligent tutoring systems are not future concepts—they are tools that can be deployed now to help teachers reach students at different paces and levels,” he said.

“The policy foundation is there. What we need is to accelerate implementation so that AI becomes part of daily instruction, not just a subject taught in schools,” he added. “The sooner we find ways to bring that into daily instruction, the more our students stand to gain.”

READ: CitizenWatch demands data storage laws amidst surge in AI usage

To properly integrate digital technology into the education system, Belmonte said teachers will need training programs to learn how to use new tools, while more public schools will require devices to take advantage of improved connectivity.

School curricula will also need “tighter, more frequent check-ins” to keep pace with technological developments.

“These are challenges where the private technology sector can be a partner of education,” Belmonte said.
